differences: documents vs chunks: the in-memory rows rank whole documents; the served index holds 117212 chunks (app/chunking (structure-aware); a .txt file takes the fixed window, 512 characters with 50 overlap), and a served document ranks at its best chunk

depth: the API returns at most 50 chunks, so a served ranking holds at most 50 documents and its Recall@50 counts within those chunks; the in-memory rows fuse 100 + 100 candidates into 100 documents (RRF k 60), the served statement 50 + 50 into 50 chunks
lexical leg: in-memory Okapi BM25 (Lucene-style English analyzer, k1 0.9, b 0.4) vs Postgres ts_rank_cd over to_tsvector('english') with the query terms OR-joined

dense leg: in-memory exact cosine over whole-document vectors (the BEIR cache) vs pgvector over chunk vectors with {'hnsw.ef_search': 100, 'hnsw.iterative_scan': 'strict_order'} per statement, through the HNSW index when the planner picks it (the plan block)

query form: the served embedder puts 'Represent this question for searching relevant passages: ' before each query on the dense leg (HuggingFaceEmbedding._model.prompts (sentence-transformers), the 'query' one used by get_query_embedding); each served row is paired with the in-memory row named '<row>+served-query-prompt', which puts the same text before the query on its dense leg, and also compared with the bare-query row of that name, which embeds the query alone; the lexical legs and the rerankers read the bare query on both sides

router: the served path routes every query ({'semantic': 584, 'lexical_path': 22, 'aggregation_query': 42}); lexical_path skips the query embedding and the reranker, aggregation_query skips the reranker; the in-memory rows have no router
rejected files: the served scanner rejected 40 documents ({'empty': 38, 'duplicate_content': 2}); judged documents among them: 1 (['117276'])

reranker input: the served reranker reads chunk text, the in-memory reranker whole documents; served BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 fp16, max_length 512, depth 20; in-memory BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 fp16, max_length 512, depth 20

bootstrap.method: percentile bootstrap over queries, one index matrix shared by all configs (paired deltas)

hardware.storage: corpus files and the Postgres data directory on node-local disk (the run's scratch directory)
